footnote: Held-out tasks are our own, built from openly licensed published data, each checking the same capability as one Terminal-Bench-Science task without reusing its data. Task names, data and graders are kept private so the set cannot be trained or tuned against; only aggregate scores are published. Every arm ran the same 45 held-out tasks, one run per task, scored pass/fail (reward 1). Runs that ended in an infrastructure or provider error were re-attempted; graded runs were not. The codex arm used vals.ai-style settings (8 h agent limit, 1 run per task, infra errors re-attempted). The three examples below are retired development sets (iterated on, so no longer blind) shown for illustration.

original.data: ICU-style EHR tables (patients, admissions, labevents, prescriptions, icustays, chartevents, dictionaries)
original.asks: Flag every row holding a data-entry error: impossible values or values contradicting the same patient's other records. Recall must be complete, precision above a floor.

heldout.data: Synthea synthetic outpatient cohort (Walonoski et al., JAMIA 2018, doi:10.1093/jamia/ocx079) with documented injected errors
heldout.schema: Different schema: patients, encounters, observations, medications, conditions, procedures, immunizations
heldout.asks: Same audit and scoring rule on a source with different tables, codes and conventions.

examples.capability: Meta-analysis effect reconstruction from source articles

original.data: Snyder (2013) meta-analysis of executive function in major depression; source articles fetched by DOI
original.asks: Reconstruct each study's effect sizes from the full texts under the meta-analysis's coding rules.

heldout.data: A published meta-analysis of memory and attention after COVID-19 (Acta Psychologica 2023, doi:10.1016/j.actpsy.2023.103838); open-access source articles fetched by DOI
heldout.schema: Different disease, tests, table layouts and reporting styles (SE, medians/IQR, subgroups)
heldout.asks: Same reconstruction task and grading style on a different literature.

examples.capability: Imaging mass cytometry of the tumour–immune interface

original.data: Melanoma biopsies before anti-PD-1, imaging mass cytometry single-cell table + masks + RECIST outcomes (26 patients)
original.asks: Label unlabelled clusters, then quantify the tumour–immune interface and relate it to response.

heldout.data: Moldoveanu et al., Science Immunology 2022 (doi:10.1126/sciimmunol.abi5072): melanoma IMC before checkpoint blockade, 30 patients
heldout.schema: Different panel, cohort, therapies (anti-CTLA-4 / anti-PD-1 / both) and irRC outcomes
heldout.asks: Same analysis on an independent cohort and antibody panel.
